country.comment: Study investigates Qwaqwa within the Maluti-a-Phofung Local Municipality, Free State Province, South Africa.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF p. 3, Section 2

effect_estimate.comment: Mixed-methods descriptive/forensic findings without inferential regression estimates, CIs, or p-values; exact descriptive quantitative indicators and audit/procurement figures reported in text are extracted. Note that the Abstract refers to '1500 delivered tankers out of 5000 paid' whereas Section 4.3.1 specifies 'R50 million for 5000 communal water storage tanks, of which only 1500 were delivered'.
effect_estimate.value: Descriptive mixed-methods findings (no inferential statistical effect estimate reported): Severe climatic deficits (17 consecutive months of negative SPI6; 45-month negative SPI12 in 2017-2020; minimum SPI3 -3.28, SPI6 -2.75, SPI12 -2.49 in January 2019) interacted with 27 months of national electricity load shedding (2015-2020), chronic infrastructure neglect (estimated 47% pipe water leakage losses, sensitivity range 30-60%), uncoordinated dual-governance land/building allocation by traditional chiefs and municipal planners (houses built over water mains and informal connections), and municipal financial mismanagement/corruption. Per capita daily water supply fell from 106 l/capita/day in 2001 to a minimum of 15 l/capita/day in 2016 and remained below basic standards at 26 l/capita/day in 2020; Fika Patso reservoir dropped to 1% capacity. Of R50 million allocated for 5,000 communal water storage tanks (described as tankers in the Abstract), only 1,500 were delivered, and despite R550 million in emergency/mitigation allocations and R600 million equitable share plus R278 million conditional grants in 2019-2020, only R42 million remained in the municipal bank account with unaccounted grant spending, driving reliance on private water tankers and exacerbating unequal water access by ability to pay.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 8-11, Sections 4.2.3-4.4.1, Figs. 4-6; PDF p. 12, Section 5.1

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 by the mixed-methods (MMAT) design ceiling. Assigned 2 because primary stakeholder interviews (including municipal water utility managers, officials, traditional leaders, and residents) triangulated with national audit reports and water-supply indicators directly document the institutional/administrative mechanisms (uncoordinated dual-governance plot/building-permission allocation over pipelines, procurement mismanagement/non-delivery of tanks, and service-area reservation of Sterkfontein Dam for Gauteng) operating on local water access.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines dual governance on tribal land where traditional chiefs exercise de facto authority to allocate plots and grant house-building permission without coordination with the municipal planning department (ELIGIBILITY: tenure, planning, building_permit; DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION: discretion, institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination), as well as institutional allocation of Sterkfontein Dam water to downstream Gauteng rather than local Qwaqwa communities (service_area).

study_design.comment: Authors explicitly describe a forensic mixed-method approach integrating qualitative interviews/desk research mapped to the Pressure-and-Release (PAR) model, quantitative hydro-climatic and water-supply indicators, and a qualitative Causal Loop Diagram (CLD).
study_design.value: Mixed-methods retrospective forensic case study combining semi-structured stakeholder interviews (conceptual and relational content analysis within the Pressure and Release framework), desk research, descriptive quantitative time-series indicator analysis, and a qualitative Causal Loop Diagram
